You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

GitType
=======

GitType turns your source code into interactive typing challenges so you can practice typing using real code from your projects or popular repositories.

Quick Install
-------------

- macOS/Linux: Use the provided installer or package manager (see releases for binary downloads).
- Nix users: run using nix run or install a packaged release.
- Alternatively, download a pre-built binary from the project's releases.

Quick Start
-----------

- Run the command and point it at a repository or the current directory to start a typing session.

  gittype                  # use current directory
  gittype /path/to/repo    # use a specific path
  gittype --repo owner/name

Documentation
-------------

This repository contains user-facing documentation describing how to use the tool. Implementation details, build instructions, and developer-focused documentation have been removed to protect internal design and implementation.

License
-------

This project is released under the terms in the LICENSE file.

--- USAGE ---
Usage
=====

git type - Basic usage and examples

- Start using the tool in the current folder:
  gittype

- Point at another path:
  gittype /path/to/project

- Practice with a remote repository:
  gittype --repo owner/repo

This document intentionally omits any implementation, build, or development instructions.

--- IMAGE DOCS ---
# GitType Banner Images

This directory contains the banner images used in the project.

## Files

- `gittype-banner.png` - Main banner image (1200x630px, OGP-ready)
- `gittype-banner.svg` - Vector version of the banner
- `banner-source.sh` - Shell script that generates the banner content

## Regenerating the Banner

To regenerate the banner images, use the following commands:

### Dependencies
```bash
npm install -g oh-my-logo
go install github.com/charmbracelet/freeze@latest
```

### PNG Banner (1200x630px - OGP ready)
```bash
freeze --execute "docs/images/banner-source.sh" \
  -o docs/images/gittype-banner.png \
  --theme "Dracula" \
  --window \
  --background="#1e1e2e" \
  --margin 10 \
  --padding 40 \
  --border.radius 15 \
  --font.family "Ubuntu Mono" \
  --font.size 22 \
  --width 1200 \
  --height 630
```

### SVG Banner
```bash
freeze --execute "docs/images/banner-source.sh" \
  -o docs/images/gittype-banner.svg \
  --theme "Dracula" \
  --window \
  --background="#1e1e2e" \
  --margin 10 \
  --padding 40 \
  --border.radius 15 \
  --font.family "Ubuntu Mono" \
  --font.size 22 \
  --width 1200 \
  --height 630
```

## Banner Design

The banner features:
- GitType ASCII logo with purple gradient generated by `oh-my-logo`
- Project tagline: "Show your AI who's boss: just you, your keyboard, and your coding sins"
- Feature highlights with ASCII icons: [*] Addictive gameplay [>] Real-time feedback [+] Track your progress
- Installation commands for brew and usage
- GitHub repository URL
- Terminal-style appearance with window controls and dark Dracula theme background
- Ubuntu Mono font for optimal readability and emoji compatibility

    def help(self, command='', long=True):
        if command.endswith('help'):
            return f"{DESCRIPTIONS['help']}\n\nUsage: {self.usage(command)}\n\nArguments:\n  [COMMAND]...  Print help for the subcommand(s)\n"
        intro = (LONG_INTRO if long else SHORT_INTRO) if not command else DESCRIPTIONS[command]
        text = intro + '\n\nUsage: ' + self.usage(command) + '\n'
        if command in ('', 'cache', 'repo'):
            commands = {'': ['history','stats','export','cache','repo','trending','help'], 'cache': ['stats','clear','list','help'], 'repo': ['list','clear','play','help']}[command]
            width = max(len(x) for x in commands)
            text += '\nCommands:\n'
            for child in commands:
                key = child if not command or child=='help' else command+' '+child
                text += '  ' + child.ljust(width) + '  ' + DESCRIPTIONS[key] + '\n'
        if not command:
            if long:

Arguments:

Options:
      --repo <REPO>
          GitHub repository URL or path to clone and play with. Supports formats:
            - owner/repo
            - https://github.com/owner/repo
            - git@github.com:owner/repo.git

      --langs <LANGS>
          Filter by programming languages (comma-separated). Supported languages:
            rust, typescript, javascript, python, ruby, go, swift, kotlin, java, php, csharp, c, cpp, haskell, dart, scala, zig
            Example: --langs rust,python,typescript

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
'''
            else:
                text += '''
Arguments:

Options:

  -V, --version        Print version
'''
        elif command=='export':

Options:

  -h, --help             Print help
'''

Options:

  -h, --help   Print help
'''
        elif command=='trending':

Arguments:
  [LANGUAGE]
          Programming language to filter trending repositories.
          Supported languages: C, C#, C++, Dart, Go, Haskell, Java, JavaScript, Kotlin, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, Scala, Swift, TypeScript, Zig

  [REPO_NAME]
          Specific repository name to select from trending list

Options:
      --period <PERIOD>
          Time period for trending (daily, weekly, monthly)
          
          [default: daily]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
'''
            else:

Arguments:
  [LANGUAGE]   Programming language to filter trending repositories
  [REPO_NAME]  Specific repository name to select from trending list

Options:
      --period <PERIOD>  Time period for trending (daily, weekly, monthly) [default: daily]
  -h, --help             Print help (see more with '--help')
'''
        else:
            text += '\nOptions:\n  -h, --help  Print help\n'
        return text

    def error(self, message, command='', tip='', usage=True):
        s = 'error: ' + message + '\n'
        if tip:
            s += '\n  tip: ' + tip + '\n'
        if usage:

        s += "\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n"

    def unexpected(self, arg, command='', tip=''):

        self.error(f"unexpected argument '{arg}' found",command,tip)

    def parse_help(self, args, command=''):
        for arg in args:
            candidate = (command+' '+arg).strip()
            if arg=='help':
                command = candidate
            elif candidate in DESCRIPTIONS and 'help' not in command:
                command = candidate
            else:
                self.error(f"unrecognized subcommand '{arg}'",command)

        seen = set()

                raise ParseExit(0,self.help(command,arg=='--help'))
            if not positional and command=='' and arg in ('--version','-V'):
                raise ParseExit(0,'gittype 0.8.0\n')
            if not positional and arg=='help' and command in ('','cache','repo'):

                key,eq,val = arg.partition('=')

                    if arg.startswith('-') and not arg.startswith('--') and len(arg)>2:
                        short=arg[1]
                        if short=='h':
                            raise ParseExit(0,self.help(command,False))
                        if short=='V' and not command:
                            raise ParseExit(0,'gittype 0.8.0\n')
                        arg='-'+short
                    if key in ('--help','--version') and eq:
                        self.error(f"unexpected value '{val}' for '{key}' found; no more were expected",command)
                    tips = {'--lang':'--langs','--language':'--langs','--repos':'--repo','--reop':'--repo','--formt':'--format','--out':'--output','--output-file':'--output','--peroid':'--period','--fore':'--force'}
                    tip = f"a similar argument exists: '{tips[key]}'" if key in tips and tips[key] in options else ''

                if key in seen and key!='--langs':

                result.repo_name=arg
            else:
                self.unexpected(arg,command)

            raise ParseExit(2,self.help(command),True)

"""A small cell-based terminal renderer and keyboard event reader."""
import os
import select
import shutil
import sys

def char_width(c):
    if unicodedata.combining(c) or c in ('\u200d','\ufe0f'):
        return 0
    return 2 if unicodedata.east_asian_width(c) in ('W','F') else 1


def width(text):
    return sum(char_width(c) for c in text)


def cut(text,columns):
    out='';n=0
    for c in text:
        w=char_width(c)
        if n+w>columns:
            break
        out+=c;n+=w
    return out


NAMED_COLORS={'black':0,'red':1,'green':2,'yellow':3,'blue':4,'magenta':5,'cyan':6,'gray':7,'grey':7,'dark_gray':8,'dark_grey':8,'light_red':9,'light_green':10,'light_yellow':11,'light_blue':12,'light_magenta':13,'light_cyan':14,'white':15,'light_gray':7}


def color_escape(value,background=False):
    if value is None:

    mode=48 if background else 38
    if isinstance(value,dict):
        return f'{mode};2;{value["r"]};{value["g"]};{value["b"]}'
    if isinstance(value,(list,tuple)):
        return f'{mode};2;{value[0]};{value[1]};{value[2]}'
    idx=NAMED_COLORS.get(value.lower(),7) if isinstance(value,str) else value
    return str((40 if background else 30)+idx) if idx<8 else str((100 if background else 90)+idx-8)


class Canvas:
    def __init__(self,w,h,theme):

        self.cells=[[(' ',(None,None,False,False)) for _ in range(w)] for _ in range(h)]

    def color(self,key):
        return self.theme.get(key,key) if isinstance(key,str) else key

    def text(self,x,y,text,fg=None,bg=None,bold=False,dim=False,limit=None):
        if not 0<=y<self.h:
            return
        style=(self.color(fg),self.color(bg),bold,dim)
        n=x

        for c in text:
            if c in '\r\n':

            cw=char_width(c)
            if cw==0:

                    self.cells[y][n-1]=(previous+c,old)
                continue
            if n+cw>end:

            if n>=0:
                self.cells[y][n]=(c,style)
                if cw==2:
                    self.cells[y][n+1]=('',style)

"""A small cell-based terminal renderer and keyboard event reader."""
import os
import select
import shutil
import sys
import termios
import time
import tty
import unicodedata


def char_width(c):
    if unicodedata.combining(c) or c in ('\u200d','\ufe0f'):
        return 0
    return 2 if unicodedata.east_asian_width(c) in ('W','F') else 1


def width(text):
    return sum(char_width(c) for c in text)


def cut(text,columns):
    out='';n=0
    for c in text:
        w=char_width(c)
        if n+w>columns:
            break
        out+=c;n+=w
    return out


NAMED_COLORS={'black':0,'red':1,'green':2,'yellow':3,'blue':4,'magenta':5,'cyan':6,'gray':7,'grey':7,'dark_gray':8,'dark_grey':8,'light_red':9,'light_green':10,'light_yellow':11,'light_blue':12,'light_magenta':13,'light_cyan':14,'white':15,'light_gray':7}


def color_escape(value,background=False):
    if value is None:
        return '49' if background else '39'
    mode=48 if background else 38
    if isinstance(value,dict):
        return f'{mode};2;{value["r"]};{value["g"]};{value["b"]}'
    if isinstance(value,(list,tuple)):
        return f'{mode};2;{value[0]};{value[1]};{value[2]}'
    idx=NAMED_COLORS.get(value.lower(),7) if isinstance(value,str) else value
    return str((40 if background else 30)+idx) if idx<8 else str((100 if background else 90)+idx-8)


class Canvas:
    def __init__(self,w,h,theme):
        self.w,self.h,self.theme=w,h,theme
        self.cells=[[(' ',(None,None,False,False)) for _ in range(w)] for _ in range(h)]

    def color(self,key):
        return self.theme.get(key,key) if isinstance(key,str) else key

    def text(self,x,y,text,fg=None,bg=None,bold=False,dim=False,limit=None):
        if not 0<=y<self.h:
            return
        style=(self.color(fg),self.color(bg),bold,dim)
        n=x
        end=self.w if limit is None else min(self.w,x+limit)
        for c in text:
            if c in '\r\n':
                break
            cw=char_width(c)
            if cw==0:
                if 0<n<=self.w:
                    previous,old=self.cells[y][n-1]
                    self.cells[y][n-1]=(previous+c,old)
                continue
            if n+cw>end:
                break
            if n>=0:
                self.cells[y][n]=(c,style)
                if cw==2:
                    self.cells[y][n+1]=('',style)
            n+=cw

    def center(self,y,text,fg=None,bg=None,bold=False,dim=False,x=0,w=None):
        if w is None:w=self.w-x
        n=width(text)
        self.text(x+max(0,(w-n+1)//2),y,text,fg,bg,bold,dim,limit=w)

    def box(self,x,y,w,h,title=''):
        if w<2 or h<2:return
        self.text(x,y,'┌'+'─'*(w-2)+'┐','border')
        self.text(x,y+h-1,'└'+'─'*(w-2)+'┘','border')
        for j in range(y+1,y+h-1):
            self.text(x,j,'│','border');self.text(x+w-1,j,'│','border')
        if title:self.text(x+1,y,title,'border',limit=w-2)

    def clear(self,x,y,w,h):
        for j in range(max(0,y),min(self.h,y+h)):
            self.text(x,j,' '*w)

    def footer(self,text,y=None):
        if y is None:y=self.h-1
        x=max(0,(self.w-width(text)+1)//2)
        import re
        pos=x
        for part in re.split(r'(\[[^]]*\])',text):
            fg='text'
            if part.startswith('['):
                fg='key_back' if part in ('[ESC]','[Q]') else 'key_action' if part in ('[SPACE]','[ENTER]') else 'key_navigation'
            self.text(pos,y,part,fg)
            pos+=width(part)

    def tabs(self,title,labels,selected):
        self.box(0,0,self.w,3,title)
        x=1
        for i,label in enumerate(labels):
            self.text(x,1,' ')
            self.text(x+1,1,label,'title' if i==selected else None,bold=i==selected,limit=self.w-x-2)
            x+=width(label)+2
            if i+1<len(labels):
                self.text(x,1,'│');x+=1

    def encode(self):
        output=[]
        current=None
        for y,row in enumerate(self.cells):
            output.append(f'\x1b[{y+1};1H')
            for char,style in row:
                if char=='':continue
                if style!=current:
                    fg,bg,bold,dim=style
                    codes=['0',color_escape(fg),color_escape(bg)]
                    if bold:codes.append('1')
                    if dim:codes.append('2')
                    output.append('\x1b['+';'.join(codes)+'m')
                    current=style
                output.append(char)
        output.append('\x1b[0m')
        return ''.join(output)

        sys.stdout.write('\x1b[0m\x1b[?7h\x1b[?1049l\x1b[?25h')
        sys.stdout.flush()

            termios.tcsetattr(self.fd,termios.TCSADRAIN,self.original)

    def size(self):
        s=shutil.get_terminal_size((80,24))
        return max(s.columns,1),max(s.lines,1)

    def render(self,canvas):
        sys.stdout.write(canvas.encode());sys.stdout.flush()

    def keys(self,timeout=.1):

import json

        self.temp.cleanup()

            p=self.invoke(flag)
            self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr),(0,'gittype 0.8.0\n',''))
        self.assertFalse((self.home/'.gittype').exists())

        p=self.invoke('-h')
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0)
        self.assertTrue(p.stdout.startswith('A typing practice tool using your own code repositories'))
        self.assertIn('Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [REPO_PATH] [COMMAND]\n',p.stdout)
        self.assertIn("  -h, --help           Print help (see more with '--help')\n",p.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr,'')

        p=self.invoke('--help')

        self.assertIn('            - git@github.com:owner/repo.git\n',p.stdout)
        self.assertIn('      --langs <LANGS>\n',p.stdout)

        for args in [('cache','stats','--help'),('help','cache','stats'),('cache','help','stats')]:
            p=self.invoke(*args)
            self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr),(0,expected,''))

    def test_parent_requires_command(self):
        p=self.invoke('cache')
        q=self.invoke('cache','--help')
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,2)
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout,'')
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr,q.stdout)

    def test_history_stats_placeholders(self):
        for cmd in ('history','stats'):
            p=self.invoke(cmd)
            self.assertEqual(p.returncode,1)
            self.assertEqual(p.stdout,'')
            self.assertEqual(p.stderr,f'❌ {cmd.capitalize()} command is not yet implemented\n💡 This feature is planned for a future release\n')

    def test_export_preserves_values_without_creating_output(self):
        p=self.invoke('export','--format','CSV','--output','a b.json')
        self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout),(1,''))
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr,'❌ Export command is not yet implemented\n💡 Requested format: CSV\n💡 Requested output: a b.json\n💡 This feature is planned for a future release\n')
        self.assertFalse((self.path/'a b.json').exists())
        p=self.invoke('export','--format=')
        self.assertIn('💡 Requested format: \n',p.stderr)

    def test_empty_cache(self):
        p=self.invoke('cache','stats')
        self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr),(0,'Challenge Cache Statistics:\n  Cached repositories: 0\n  Total size: 0 bytes\n',''))
        self.assertEqual(self.invoke('cache','list').stdout,'No cached challenges found.\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.invoke('cache','clear').stdout,'Challenge cache cleared successfully.\n')

    def test_cache_counts_top_level_files(self):
        cache=self.home/'.gittype'/'cache';cache.mkdir(parents=True)
        (cache/'one.json').write_bytes(b'abc')

        (cache/'nested').mkdir();(cache/'nested'/'three.json').write_bytes(b'xyz')
        self.assertEqual(self.invoke('cache','stats').stdout,'Challenge Cache Statistics:\n  Cached repositories: 2\n  Total size: 15 bytes\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.invoke('cache','list').stdout,'No cached challenges found.\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.invoke('cache','clear').returncode,0)
        self.assertTrue((cache/'nested'/'three.json').exists())
        self.assertEqual(self.invoke('cache','stats').stdout,'Challenge Cache Statistics:\n  Cached repositories: 0\n  Total size: 0 bytes\n')

    def test_empty_repository_cache(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.invoke('repo','clear').stdout,'No cached repositories directory found.\n')
        (self.home/'.gittype'/'repos'/'unused-owner').mkdir(parents=True)
        self.assertEqual(self.invoke('repo','clear','--force').stdout,'No cached repositories found.\n')

    def test_language_validation_preserves_whitespace(self):
        p=self.invoke('--langs','Rust, PYTHON,wat','--langs','wat')
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,1)
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout,'')
        self.assertTrue(p.stderr.startswith('❌ Unsupported language(s):  PYTHON, wat, wat\n'))
        self.assertTrue(p.stderr.endswith('   cljs\n'))
        self.assertEqual(list(self.path.glob('gittype_error_*.log')),[])

    def test_root_parameters_do_not_apply_to_subcommands(self):
        p=self.invoke('--langs','nonsense','history')
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr,'❌ History command is not yet implemented\n💡 This feature is planned for a future release\n')
        p=self.invoke('/any/path','--repo','anything','cache','list')
        self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout),(0,'No cached challenges found.\n'))

    def test_unknown_option(self):
        p=self.invoke('--wat')
        self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout),(2,''))
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr,"error: unexpected argument '--wat' found\n\n  tip: to pass '--wat' as a value, use '-- --wat'\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] [REPO_PATH] [COMMAND]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        self.assertFalse((self.home/'.gittype').exists())

    def test_missing_value(self):
        p=self.invoke('--repo')
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,2)
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr,"error: a value is required for '--repo <REPO>' but none was supplied\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")

    def test_duplicates(self):
        p=self.invoke('export','--format','json','--format','csv')
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,2)
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr,"error: the argument '--format <FORMAT>' cannot be used multiple times\n\nUsage: executable export [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")

    def test_terminal_failure_has_diagnostic_file(self):
        p=self.invoke('/no/such/path')
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,1)
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout,'')
        self.assertRegex(p.stderr,r'^💾 Error details written to: gittype_error_\d{8}_\d{6}\.log\nError: Terminal error: Failed to create terminal: Resource temporarily unavailable \(os error 11\)\n$')
        logs=list(self.path.glob('gittype_error_*.log'))
        self.assertEqual(len(logs),1)
        content=logs[0].read_text()
        self.assertIn('ERROR TYPE: "gittype::domain::error::GitTypeError"\n',content)
        self.assertNotIn('RUST_LOG:',content)

    def test_trending_language_validation(self):
        p=self.invoke('trending','rs')
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,1)
        self.assertTrue(p.stderr.startswith("❌ Unsupported language: 'rs'\n📚 Supported languages: C, C#, C++, Dart, Go, Haskell"))
        self.assertTrue(p.stderr.endswith('Error: Validation error: Unsupported language: rs\n'))

if __name__=='__main__':
    unittest.main()

        rows=self.frame()
        self.assertEqual([i for i,line in enumerate(rows) if line.endswith('█')],list(range(5,12)))
        self.app.handle('RIGHT')
        self.assertIn('Score Calculation Formula:',self.frame()[4])
        self.assertEqual(self.app.help_scroll,0)

        self.assertIn('Overview (Last 7 days)',self.frame()[6])

        self.assertIn('CPM Trend',self.frame()[6])

        self.assertIn('No Repository Selected',self.frame()[8])
        self.app.handle('RIGHT')
        self.assertIn('No Language Selected',self.frame()[8])

        self.assertEqual(self.app.screen,'stage_result')
        self.assertEqual(self.app.result['keys'],25)
        self.assertEqual(self.app.result['mistakes'],0)
        self.assertEqual(self.app.result['accuracy'],100)

if __name__=='__main__':
    unittest.main()
